input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision and no change-of-control language appears elsewhere. It bars assignment without the other party's prior written approval with only an affiliate carve-out: there is no M&A/successor carve-out for Client, consent is not qualified by a reasonableness standard, and there is no bar on assignment to our competitors. That fails the fallback and approaches walk-away territory, since a merger or sale of substantially all assets would require TrueLink's discretionary approval. One short inserted sentence supplies the successor carve-out, the not-unreasonably-withheld standard on our consent, the competitor bar, and confirmation that a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination right, leaving the existing mutual consent baseline and affiliate carve-out intact.

ops.text: No such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Client's approval of any assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld; TrueLink shall not assign or transfer to a competitor of Client; and no change of control of Client shall give TrueLink any right to terminate this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a consent-free carve-out for our assignments to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, a reasonableness standard on our consent to a TrueLink assignment with no assignment to our competitors, and confirmation that a change of control of Client gives TrueLink no termination right. The existing mutual consent requirement and affiliate carve-out are untouched.
proposal.summary: Add Client successor carve-out, reasonableness standard and competitor bar on TrueLink assignment, and no termination on Client change of control.
